title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-07
body:
2026-03-04 (WIP) - morning scratchpad

Top of mind:
- Rolling capacity alert last night (02:15 UTC) for eu-west-1-gpu-pool. Autoscaler bumped but some pods stuck Pending ~10m. Need to check kube events and node provisioning logs.
- Follow up with cloud on noisy neighbor / slow EBS attach in that AZ — saw 4x attach latency.
- Confirmed 2x model-serving pods OOM during long 4k sequences. Possibly KV cache leak or incorrect max_cache_size.

TODO (high priority)
- [ ] Investigate eu-west-1-gpu-pool Pending root cause (kubectl describe, controller logs) — target EOD.
- [ ] Add autoscaler fallback: if provisioning > 5m route to rdw-small-a100 variant (can accept longer latency) — prototyping YAML in PR #814.
- [ ] Patch node image to kernel 5.15.102 (ROCE fix) on staging (gnode-*/staging) and run soak for 24h.
- [ ] Reconcile GPU inventory spreadsheet with actual node labels (a100-80gb vs a100-40gb) — update capacity plan.
- [ ] Postmortem notes for last-night incident (link to INC-1234) — start draft.

Quick notes / commands used:
- kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
- kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>  # check pv claims + events
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=redwood-gpu" --zones eu-west-1a
- ssh gnode-13 && sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 200
- nvidia-smi dmon -s u  # check sustained power draw on suspect node

Observations:
- Node gnode-13 showed abnormal attach latency (dmesg shows ext4 mount timeout at 02:10). EBS metrics show spike in queue length. Suspect cloud provider incident.
- Two serving containers OOMed at ~03:02 while processing 4096 token sequences. Memory accounting: container limit 140GB but process peaked 150GB. Need to add guardrails: limit model KV cache growth OR drop default max_seq to 3072 for that model.

Config notes to change (draft YAML snippets in PR):
- autoscaler: 
  - scaleUpTimeout: 300s -> 360s for cross-AZ provisioning
  - fallbackPolicy: routeTo: rdw-small-a100
- serving runtime: 
  - model.default_max_seq: 3072 (temporary)
  - kv_cache.max_entries: 256k -> cap by bytes not entries

Follow-ups / people to ping:
- Marcus: confirm node image rollout window and kernel OTA schedule.
- Sasha: ask infra-cloud for EBS attach logs + ticket update.
- SRE-oncall: visibility into autoscaler decisions (trace id 0x7a3b2)

Notes to self (messy):
- remember: when testing kv cache leak, run long-run with continuous query (1000 inferences per min) and monitor /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS over 6h.
- possible fix: free cache shards after inactive timeout 300s (but must ensure correctness for multi-request contexts).
- check PR #789 (serving-runtime) for recent mem allocator change — could be related.

Meeting prep (30m with Marcus @ 11:00):
- bring atlas of nodes (counts by instance type) — need numbers for capacity commit next quarter
- discuss short term workaround (route traffic to smaller model variant vs increase capacity) and cost tradeoffs

Scratch TODO (low priority)
- [ ] write short runbook for node reprovisioning when NVLINK firmware mismatch detected
- [ ] add monitoring alert for sustained attach latency > 3s (currently only >10s)
- [ ] tidy up capacity spreadsheet (link in linked_artifacts)

Questions / unknowns:
- Is the memory accounting bug only hitting specific a100-80gb kernel? need to cross-check older nodes.
- Can we safely cap kv cache by bytes rather than entries without regression? quick benchmark planned after lunch.

End notes:
- Keep this doc short — move polished timelines and postmortem to shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/incidents/INC-1234-postmortem when draft ready.
- If I get paged, follow checklist above and ping Marcus + SRE-oncall.

-- Avery
